claim: In the explicitly declared exact-integer translated-local-PN interpretation, every finite L_N has a uniformly constructed complete prepared context/color family whose actual C0 projection is its indexed point. One typed native WG constructor handles arbitrary finite patterns, palettes and word lengths, computed in-region selection or certified refusal, retained input/program/request histories and variable-word substitution. Full local reference data agree under cutoff restriction and under an explicit local identifier renaming with tested legacy contexts. This does not identify the exact interpretation with the entire intended operational space or make the Number-valued sector API unbounded.
source_operations: Exact integer translation of the existing canonical P/N local template, its shared face and five-coordinate PN permutation. Root references are e0,e1,e2,e3 and -e0+e1+e3. No new geometric move or monochromatic seed is admitted.
uniform_region: Enumerate every integer triple in [-N,N]^3 with even sum. The inverse zero-sum barycentric shift is (-(x+y+z),x+y-z,x+z-y,y+z-x)/2. Give an all-index coverage/uniqueness/termination argument, not a conclusion from radius samples.
formal_boundary: Kernel checks exact derived references, actual point binding, full five-slot permutation, uniform bounded membership, native program and point/color readouts, and projected variable-word substitution. Completeness of the D3 parametrization and agreement with the declared local geometry/PN API are all-index written arguments plus independent exact replay, not kernel interpretation of JS.
rivals: A declared point remains independent of its context
Opaque local IDs are silently identified across namespaces
Safe machine samples are extrapolated to unbounded Number geometry
controls: change outside C2 while preserving C0
stop_condition: Record only the exact-source interpretation theorem. Keep the existing parent open if its operation-preserving interpretation into the intended space is not supplied; add no fixed-cutoff leaf and do not treat machine arithmetic refusal as a mathematical counterexample.
